A1.justification: Both PDFs describe E2Former and Wigner 6j convolution. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable, and shared methods and experiments provide clear comparison anchors despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original runtime benchmarks, E2Former energy and force predictions on OC20, OC22, and SPICE, and a 253-atom molecular-dynamics simulation.

after.justification: v3 retains original E2Former results and adds QM9 predictions, large-system efficiency measurements, water-cluster simulations, and a solvated-Chignolin evaluation.

M1.justification: v3 Algorithm 1 adds pairwise-distance computation and degree-dependent attention normalization, alpha^(k) = alpha/D^k; v1 applies alpha directly. This revises the written computation within the retained binomial-expansion and Wigner-recoupling procedure. The expanded architectural descriptions do not establish that every newly described component was newly implemented.

E1.justification: v3 retains OC20, OC22, SPICE, and the pretraining corpora, but adds QM9 evaluation on U0, HOMO, and LUMO. It also adds pure-water molecular dynamics and solvated-Chignolin optimization cases beyond v1's solvated-amino-acid simulation, substantially extending the evaluated tasks and molecular systems.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged. New comparisons introduce GotenNet and the original Equiformer on QM9, compare E2Former against MACE-Large and EquiformerV2 for system-level efficiency, and use MACE alongside MADFT in the large-water simulation. These substantially expand the evaluated comparison methods and their participation.

E3.justification: v3 adds a matched-configuration EquiformerV2 comparison using 12 layers, Lmax=3, and Mmax=2. New protocols include angular-order and neighbor-count sweeps on 1,000-node graphs, plus memory and throughput measurements across 200–6,400 atoms. The original benchmark settings and hyperparameter table are retained; these additions do not establish reruns of those experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's graph-size scaling and small-system simulation, v3 tests sensitivity to angular order and neighborhood size, examines model-level memory limits, and adds a matched-configuration comparison. Figure 6 also provides Chignolin optimization trajectories and element-specific force-error analyses. These address substantial additional efficiency and applicability questions.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its results. v3's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting but introduces no uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values. New results include QM9 scores, 6,400-atom throughput of 0.59 samples/second at 80 GB, and Chignolin force error of 0.484 kcal/mol/angstrom. Figure 3 changes the MADFT timing bar from approximately 45 to 180 while retaining the stated simulation setup. Table 7 adds comparison results, but its E/F labels assign the same E2Former values oppositely to Table 1, making their interpretation inconsistent.

T1.justification: v3 explicitly defines solid harmonics as R(l)(r)=|r|^l Y(l)(r-hat), substantially expands the binomial and recoupling proofs, and introduces ordering-invariance and projection results. It also adds formal equivariance, channel/order-dependent complexity, and many-body-reduction lemmas in Appendices D–G. These are substantive mathematical additions, although some new arguments contain internal inconsistencies.

C1.justification: The central E2Former contribution and 7–30-fold convolution-speedup claim remain. v3 qualifies the linear-time framing as linear-scaling tensor products, changes the introduction and conclusion's benchmark-accuracy claim from state-of-the-art to competitive, and extends the molecular-dynamics outperformance claim to EGNNs.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges that the complete attention model is not strictly linear and explains reallocating computational savings toward model expressivity. It qualifies QM9 performance by emphasizing the intended large-system application. Its checklist additionally mentions small-graph inefficiency and ideal molecular geometries, limitations not stated in v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link and extensive Appendix H documentation covering embeddings, normalization, attention construction, configurable feed-forward modules, and gated aggregation across orders. These substantially expand implementation information beyond v1's diagram, pseudocode, and hyperparameter table. The original hyperparameter values remain unchanged; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: The invariant, Cartesian-equivariant, and spherical-equivariant taxonomy remains. v3 adds references including GotenNet, PaiNN, ViSNet, universality results, and kernelized attention, and introduces a comparison between scalarization efficiency and tensor-product completeness. This refines the existing positioning rather than replacing it.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the introduction and mathematical exposition, moves related work after the experiments, consolidates architecture discussion, and relocates Algorithm 1 to Appendix B. The former single appendix becomes organized Appendices A–J with a contents page, alongside a new checklist. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: v3 changes the two-column presentation to a single-column layout, redraws the method overview, and expands the runtime figure with additional panels. It adds water-cluster and Chignolin figures and three experimental tables. Existing architecture, glossary, and hyperparameter displays are retained but relocated and rescaled.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical coverage, implementation documentation, and claim calibration. However, its new Appendix D.6 counts binomial multiplicities both through a coefficient and through the explicit ordering sum, while Lemma G.1 replaces neighborhood aggregation with global aggregation without restricting the graph accordingly. Table 7 also has conflicting energy/force labeling. These additions affect theoretical guarantees and interpretation of new evidence, leaving the net quality direction uncertain despite clear benefits.
